notes.inflation: Inflation is Pakistan's national consumer price index as the IMF republishes it: the change in the all-items index on twelve months, and on the previous month. There is no interest rate on this page: the State Bank of Pakistan's data service does not allow automated downloads, and no international body republishes its policy rate.
notes.labour: Unemployment is the International Labour Organization's modelled annual estimate, published by the World Bank, not the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics' own survey figure, shown from 2012: before that the modelled series reads under 1%, far below the surveys. GDP and growth are annual, from the World Bank, for Pakistan's fiscal years (July to June, labelled by the year in which they end); Pakistan's quarterly national accounts are not available to automated downloads.
notes.trade: Goods trade is Pakistan's monthly data as the IMF republishes it, in rupees, as Pakistan reports it, shown from July 2022: the IMF's series has no figures for November 2021 to June 2022. Exports are valued free on board, imports including cost, insurance and freight. The IMF publishes it some months after the month it covers.
notes.public: Debt and the budget balance are the IMF World Economic Outlook's general government figures, actual years only, so estimates and projections never appear as data. Pakistan's budget years run July to June.
notes.markets: The exchange rate is the World Bank's annual average official rate, shown from 1982, when the rupee's fixed link to the US dollar ended and a managed float began. There is no 10-year government bond yield or business confidence index on this page.
